    Friday 28 August 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    20 leads signed by a live pre-open sixteen-seat board under a Mix mandate — ten stock and ten option, with every contract clearing the chair's own three vetoes and the three nickel calls kept off the option ladder by where they were ranked

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). Regime is risk-on and thin: SPY 771.10 is +0.66% on the day and +1.11% on five, QQQ +1.37%, IWM flat, VIX 14.48 and down 4.3% on the week - while the room's own FFT composite projects -1.47% over the next ten sessions. Tape and cycle disagree; I am sizing for the tape and writing kills for the cycle. THE COMPOSITE. Last night's court found against me and the finding was correct: I published 44-84 off seat medians running 47-57, a 2.88x stretch that scored rho -0.094 against the day's moves while the RAW medians scored -0.011 and the plain mean +0.035. I degraded the ordering I derived from. Today the composite is the MEDIAN of the fifteen filed sheets, computed per candidate, with ties broken in a declared order - the plain mean of the fifteen, then the Oracle, then the Skeptic. The published number is a STRICTLY MONOTONE map of that composite: it stretches the spacing and cannot touch the ordering, so today's rank correlation is identical to the median's whatever it turns out to be. Inversions against the median: NINE, every one of them a named chair's dissent, listed below and repeated in that lead's own summary. Unnamed inversions: zero. THE DISSENT, nine moves. UP, all five for the same reason - the pyramid leader's names taken as common because their tickets are vetoed or unusable: CMI 21->3, MCD 36->8, WMT 31->9, KO 24->13, NKE 38->16. DOWN, all four because they are second and third costumes of a bet already in the book, or a thesis the tape contradicts: COP 10->22, COIN 17->21, HOOD 11->26, URI 16->30. THE GATE. Twelve leads print 60 or better this morning and none of that is evidence. On raw medians only NVDA (63) clears 60 and ELEVEN names tie at exactly 50. The >=60 spotlight today is a rank presentation, not a conviction threshold - read it as the top eight by rank and nothing more.

    WHAT THE MEDIAN IS ACTUALLY MEASURING, and this is the defect I take to tonight's court rather than hide this morning: eleven of forty names sit at a median of exactly 50 because two seats parked there. The Watchdog filed the literal number 50 on 29 of 40 rows (sd 2.5, whole range 45-55) and the Domestic Desk on 22 of 40; 47 of the sheet's 600 grades are exactly 50. A median is robust to outliers and defenceless against mass abstention at the centre. On half my book the ordering was chosen by the seats that declined to have an opinion, not by the ones that did. THE ROOM'S DISAGREEMENT is not noise, and it is not about direction - it is about INSTRUMENT. The Oracle wears the crown today (rank 1, equity 101,771, tier 1) and grades a defensive shares book: MCD 82, BAC 80, WMT 79, XOM 76, KO 74, CMI 70, NKE 66 - and refuses, in writing, every ticket attached to them: "size that leg at zero and buy the 260.06 shares." The flow, momentum and gap seats grade the chains and refuse the businesses: the crown files 22 on NVDA, 12 on CRWD, 8 on PLTR and 8 on COIN, the four names the room ranks highest. Under a ten-stock and ten-option book I do not have to choose between them and I have not - the crown's names are the SHARE half and the room's names are the OPTION half. That is the largest structural decision in this book. Note also, on the record, that the crown is a paper-P&L ranking and not a calibration ranking: the Oracle's grade-return correlation is +0.174 over 140 grades, fourth of fifteen, while the Skeptic's +0.254 on a 0.786 hit rate is the best number in the room - and the Skeptic did most of today's instrument work for me. THE OVERRULE. I invoked the instrument rule and the owner's ten-and-ten overruled me; the option half then returned +11.19% on the premium while the shares lost 0.19%. One four-hour sample from the same wrapper that cost 35.93% the session before: mean -12.37%, sd 33.3. What survived that court is the LIQUIDITY half, and today it bites five times. The MCD $290C at $0.15, the BAC $63C at $0.13 and the KO $91C at $0.31 fail the $0.50 premium veto; ULTA's 09-18 500P (66 lots) and ADSK's 09-18 240P (74 lots) fail the hundred-lot realisability floor. All five names are graded into the share half or out of the book entirely, so the slate cannot reach those contracts at all - the way to keep a vetoed ticket out of the book is to keep its name off the option ladder, not to hope the scanner declines it. The options tape is live, so the instrument rule does not apply today in any case, and the book is the owner's ten and ten. THE HORIZON SPLIT is ten swing and ten position/long-term, and ZERO intraday, which is short of the mandate's three and is deliberate. Every contract inside the 0-5 DTE window expires this afternoon except AVGO's 08-31, which is one session away - all of them fail the three-sessions-to-expiry veto. Rather than mislabel a dividend-and-fear position as a day trade to fill a counter, I file the intraday quota unmet with its reason on the record.

    ONE BET IN MANY COSTUMES. Forty rows are about six bets, so a ten-option book cannot be ten independent ideas and I will not present correlation as diversification. CRUDE: XOM and COP printed matching deep-ITM 09-18 structures in exact round lots of 1,200 and 2,400 on the same morning - one financing program across two tickers, not two bulls - and 78% of XOM's call tape is struck 20-36% below spot. XOM carries it, in shares; COP gets no slot. CRYPTO/FINTECH: XYZ carries it as the only one of the three whose chain the room verified at strike level; COIN and HOOD are out. SOFTWARE GAPS: eight names, and CRWD carries it on the least-extended oscillator (RSI 64.0 after +20.50%); CRM's catalyst has already paid to RSI 80.1 with an empty resistance list and support 17.03% below, so it gets nothing. SEMIS: NVDA carries it and AVGO is the single second expression I allow, on the only positive model print of forty. Ranks 6-10 of the option ladder are second copies of bets already sitting in ranks 1-5. Size them as one bet.

    THE NET IS NOT CONSULTED TODAY. The model prints negative on 39 of 40 tickers, including -113.04% on MRNA and -38.03% on CRM. That is not a bearish forecast, it is a broken one, and last night's retrain made the population worse. AVGO's +1.25 is noted as the only positive print and weighted as a curiosity, not as evidence.

    THE TWO I DEFEND HARDEST. NVDA, because it is the only leg on the sheet that genuinely fills - 5.00M open interest, the 09-04 235C at $2.25 trading 138,847 against 137,917 open - and because RSI 61.4 after +8.74% is an unspent oscillator. Its defect is stated in its own summary: break-even 237.25 sits above the 235.47 swing high, so the trade must clear its only resistance to return zero. And CMI, which I moved eighteen ranks: RSI 31.5 is the lowest of forty, the 571.62 kill is 0.39% away and was approached over several sessions rather than manufactured inside one, and there is a dated demand wire on the customer. Every seat that marked CMI down marked down the chain, which is an instrument objection, and on a book with ten share slots it does not bite.

    WHAT MAKES THIS BOOK WRONG. The option half is long QQQ beta in five costumes - NVDA, AVGO, MSFT, META, CRWD - into a -1.47% ten-day cycle projection with VIX at 14.5, and if the gap-ups mean-revert they lose together and the premium halves before any of them reaches a stop. AVGO carries an undated earnings binary inside both expiries and this packet ships no calendar to rule it out. And the share half is essentially one seat's book: if the Oracle is early rather than right, MCD, WMT, KO and NKE all sit there collecting dividends while the tape runs away from them. The single number that falsifies the morning is SPY through 766.08, the lower lip of today's gap - that kills the option half's premise wholesale, and it is the level I want the desk watching. HOUSE RULES, decided now and not mid-session. STAKES: flat weights, no rank-sizing - the rolling five-session rank correlation is still negative and rank has not earned the right to set size. One unit per lead, and the five QQQ-beta costumes share ONE unit between them, not five. The option half is half a unit each: a mean of -12.37% at sd 33.3 is the honest prior on this wrapper. EXITS: every option lead is dead at -50% of premium or at the end of its stated horizon, whichever comes first, and no leg is rolled - a roll is a new trade that has to be graded tomorrow morning like everything else. Every share lead is dead at its named kill. RATCHETS: NVDA and CRWD carry them, being the two highest-variance ideas in the top ranks - at +50% on the premium, sell half and let the remainder run to expiry with a stop at entry. Variance is harvested, never averaged into. WINDFALL: any leg that doubles is cut to a free carry the same session and the proceeds do not fund a new position today. And the intraday quota stays unmet - I will not buy a same-day ticket to fill a counter.

Collector data is real and timestamped. Nothing here came from the app's mock path: the 3-second automatic run that fired at 07:02 ET was discarded before this book was written.

    What the board did not know
    1. Congressional disclosure printed 0 buys / 0 sells / 0 politicians on all forty names for the ELEVENTH consecutive session — including NVDA, PLTR, BAC and GS. The Watchdog filed that this is not credible as truth rather than reading it as an all-clear, abstained at 50 on 29 names, and moved only the eleven it could attach to a dated, ticker-naming federal document.
    2. The packet's option VOLUME is yesterday's while OPEN INTEREST has already absorbed it. The Herald proved it on CRWD's 09/04 $240C: 8,273 lots against 282 open interest reads as 29.3x, but the same volume against today's 4,171 open interest is 1.98x — about 3,889 lots stayed open. Any freshness ratio computed off this packet without that correction is overstated.
    3. Several headline call/put ratios are deep in-the-money financing artifacts, not demand. Flow, Dagger and the Herald independently found the same fingerprint on XOM's 8.76 (about 95,300 of 122,159 call contracts struck 20-36%% in the money against open interest of 1 to 245), and it voids AMGN, COP, WMT and BA as well.
    4. No ATR field shipped in the candidate packet, so the stop/target bracket here is computed off the 20-bar swing range and the Glazier's window multiples are flagged estimates.
    Contracts the desk could not transact
    1. nickels_kept_out — MCD, BAC and KO carry the three sub-dollar calls in the packet ($0.15, $0.13, $0.31). Ten of the fifteen seats priced them as lottery tickets — the Chartist computed that MCD's $290C needs +11.57%% against 1.75%% of measured room, BAC's +3.20%% against 0.46%%, KO's +2.52%% against 0.02%% — and the Oracle graded the businesses high while calling the contracts what they are. All three are in the book as SHARES.
    2. vetoes_applied — All ten contracts pass the chair's three vetoes and the scanner's own bounds (min 6 DTE, min 100 open interest, strike within 15%% of spot, last price above $0.05). Thinnest: COST 2026-09-18 $910P at 1,952 open interest. Cheapest: MRNA 2026-09-04 $125P at $0.99.

    House rules
    1. Final grades are the MEDIAN of the fifteen seat grades. The chair reports the published ladder is a strictly monotone map of that median — zero unnamed inversions, nine named chair's dissents — after last night's court found its 2026-08-27 stretch scored rho -0.094 against outcomes while the raw medians it came from scored -0.011.
    2. Ten stock leads and ten option leads. The owner's standing house rule, restated this morning, and the run now ASSERTS it after the fact rather than trusting the slate builder: a book that quietly ships 13/7 because some lead had no pickable contract is a broken promise that looks like a normal run.
    3. Every option leg clears the three vetoes the chair committed to at the 2026-08-26 court — premium at or above $0.50, open interest at or above 250, at least three sessions to expiry. Cheapest premium $0.99 (MRNA 09/04 $125P), thinnest book 1,952 open interest (COST 09/18 $910P), nearest expiry 7 sessions.
    4. The three sub-dollar calls the packet offered — MCD 09/18 $290C at $0.15, BAC 09/04 $63C at $0.13, KO 09/04 $91C at $0.31 — are NOT in the book as options. All three names are, as SHARES, at ranks 8, 12 and 13. The chair kept them off the option ladder by where it ranked them rather than by hoping the scanner would decline them, which is the difference between a rule and a wish.
    5. Stop and target are the house bracket off the 'aggressive' risk profile — 2.0 ATR to the stop, 4.0 ATR to the target — anchored on the entry. A table, not a judgement.
    6. No lead carries a written invalidation: the Executive's output schema still has no field for one, so the Bailiff has nothing to police on this book either.

    The court's report

    Run 26 — a FULL session. The packet froze at 07:25 ET, pre-open, so unlike last night there is no four-hour excuse anywhere in this document.

    EVERY CONSTRUCTION LOST TO DOING NOTHING. Flat twenty lines returned -0.095%. The published top five returned -1.098%, the raw median's -1.086%, the plain mean's -0.788%. The ranking did not merely fail to add value — it selected the worse half of the board's own book. The ten names sent to the option ladder averaged -0.863% on the underlying; the ten left in shares made +0.673%. NVDA 92. The chair's highest grade of the week, and its 09/04 $235C lost 84.0% of premium on a -4.57% underlying. CRWD's $240C lost 73.98%, XYZ's $88C 66.97%, INTU's $300P 48.6%. Every one of those contracts passed the chair's three liquidity vetoes: the losses were direction, not fillability, so the rule that was written after 8/26 addressed a different failure than the one that arrived.

    THE THREE-SESSION OPTION RECORD, which is the only honest way to read tonight: -35.93%, +11.19%, -29.34%. Mean about -18%, and the sign flips every session. The Skeptic filed the correct read LAST NIGHT, before the tape agreed with it — 'two four-hour samples with opposite signs are not evidence about an instrument' — while other seats were calling the owner's overrule vindicated. What three samples establish is the VARIANCE, not the sign.

    THE CHAIR'S CORRECTION WORKED, ON ONE SESSION. Convicted last night of a 2.88x stretch that scored -0.094 against raw medians at -0.011, it published a strictly monotone map of the median with nine named dissents; tonight that scored -0.187 against the median's -0.422 and the mean's -0.351. Two sessions, opposite verdicts, and nobody gets to claim a method from either.

    THE MACHINERY MOVED. The fund's allocation model was diagnosed and repaired today: it had been assigning every new candidate a weight of exactly zero since 2026-08-21, because a corpus that is 99.1% synthetic collapsed one feature's training standard deviation to 0.0099 and the model was extrapolating 573 sigma. It admitted five lots today. For a week the board's grades were being fed to a machine that could not act on them. Separately, the pulse population's generation 10 refused its fifth consecutive child.

    The option record

    THREE SESSIONS OF THE SAME EXPERIMENT, and the room should read all three together rather than the one in front of it. 2026-08-26: option contracts -35.93% while underlyings moved -0.71%. 2026-08-27: +11.19% while shares lost 0.19%. 2026-08-28: -29.34% while shares made +0.67%. Mean about -18%, and the sign changes every session. On 8/26 and 8/27 the room argued the wrapper was the problem and was overruled by the owner's ten-and-ten house rule; on 8/27 that overrule looked vindicated and the room said so. Tonight it looks wrong again. A seat that concludes 'options are bad' from three samples is doing the same bad inference as one that concluded 'options are good' last night. What is actually established is the VARIANCE, not the sign — and variance on a ten-line half of a twenty-line book is a sizing question, which is the owner's, not an instrument question, which would be yours.

    Flowconviction32

    On base. MSFT was the one thing in the option half that worked and it was my top grade. I gave it 68 and called it "the cleanest footprint on the sheet": 505C at 9.8x (37,633 on 3,829) struck at the $505.06 spot, 510C at 5.6x, 500C at 3.7x, "three strikes all fresh, none of them trading against a wall of stale OI," CONCENTRATION 8.1%. The desk bought the $500C and it returned +30.06% in a half that lost 29.34%. My pre-commitment: I filed ABSTAIN-BLIND-CHAIN last night and applied it by hand on six names — INTU, XYZ, MCD, KO, ULTA, SNPS. Two shipped as contracts anyway: INTU -48.60%, XYZ -66.97%, mean -57.78%. Excise them and the option half goes -29.343% to -22.23%, worth 7.11 points. Two sessions in, the flag covers four contracts — HOOD -17.22, HPQ -28.57, INTU -48.60, XYZ -66.97 — all negative, mean -40.34%, against sixteen visible chains at -1.26%. Discipline on that: a random 2-of-10 beats -57.78 in 7 of 45 draws (p=0.16), and 4-of-4 negative at a 60% base rate is p=0.13. Neither is a finding. On the three-session record I do not change my mind, and that is checkable — last night I wrote the defensible core is "this chain is blind, that one is not," not "the tape is half-down, no options." The sign flipped and my position didn't, because it was never a claim about the sign.

    Off base. NVDA. I graded it 63 bull, my second-highest; its contract lost 84.0% on a -4.57% underlying. My own note says "the freshest single row is actually the 225 PUT at 9.1x (265,915 on 29,145)" — fresher than the 230C at 5.0x or the 225C at 5.3x — and then deletes it with my 0.3 high-ATR put weight because NVDA had run +8.74% into the packet. My own rule makes freshness the spine of the grade; I overrode it with a discount I invented to explain puts away. It fired three times, wrong three times: NVDA; MRNA, cut to 47, whose $125P made +16.16%; NKE, where I withheld it, graded 28 bear, and it rose 3.02%. All four bears missed — META +1.21, WMT +0.45, NKE +3.02, BAC +1.88 — while my bulls averaged -1.45%. Inverted. On the 92: a legibility score spent as a conviction score. The footprint was real: 684,401 in the 230C, 21.5% coverage. Flow says who is positioned, never that they are right, and my grade carried no magnitude — the $235C needed +4.07% in five sessions and I never wrote that number. My token was prose, not code: INTU published at 76, XYZ at 73, both shipped. My rho, -0.255, recomputes to -0.193 on mid-ranks — six of twenty grades are the same 50, so a quarter of my sheet has no order. At n=20 the SE is 0.23: a full session leaves me 1.1 SE from zero, a coin, not a verdict.

    Lesson. Four changes, each checkable tomorrow. One: the 0.3 high-ATR put weight is dead. It fired three times today and was wrong three times. Near-money put volume counts at FULL weight regardless of the name's realized move; to discount it I must name the stock position it hedges, not the ATR. Under this NVDA grades 48, not 63, and MRNA 58, not 47. Two: every option candidate gets a STRIKE MATCH line — does the desk's contract appear in my notables? MATCH / MISS / BLIND. Today MATCH +6.24% (n=3), MISS -39.52% (n=4), BLIND -57.78% (n=2); strip NVDA and CRWD and MISS collapses to -0.04%, so the whole gap is two names. I am printing it to be scored over thirty contracts, not claiming it works. Three: every grade above 60 carries the breakeven — (strike+premium)/spot as a percent and trading sessions to expiry. NVDA: +4.07% in 5. MSFT: +2.13% in 15. Four: tomorrow I check whether the chair's median actually drops ABSTAIN-BLIND-CHAIN rows. If it does not, I stop writing 50 and file a null, because a rule that lives in a comment field is not a rule.

    Daggerconviction28

    On base. Full session, pre-open freeze, no four-hour excuse. Three things held, and two of them are my own rules applied by hand. ULTA: 60/bear on c/p 0.64 (z -1.71) and a rejection 0.35% under the 0.236 fib at 541.98 -- returned +4.18%, the best line in the twenty, while the chair ranked it 18th at 52. MRNA: my 2x-200d cap says no short above 2x clears 40 until the reversal prints; MRNA at 2.79x, the -4.60% print, cap lifted by hand and stamped UNCODED in the note. It earned +3.35% and the 09-04 125P +16.16% -- the only option line in the book that made money. Rule two also earned: I withheld the range-position handle from AVGO and said it "cost this name about four points," and AVGO returned -0.74%, so demoting a loser helped the ordering; the same consistency cost CMI fifteen points and CMI returned -1.57%. XOM: the denominator-artifact check held -- 39,602 lots on the 09-18 120C at $40.19 against 245 open interest is stock replacement, flow signal zero -- and XOM closed +0.17%, dead flat, against my 33 and the chair's 53.
